source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice mcqs written from Unit 8 (PDF 234-255), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh Unit 8 (Numerical Solutions of Nonlinear Equations (TOC: 'Numerical Method')) ke poore unit se practice MCQs hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein. Har sawal ka aik sahi jawab hai aur saath mukhtasar wajah, jis mein hal ke qadam diye gaye hain.
8.1 Basic Principles of Approximating Real Roots of Nonlinear Equations

blocks.prompt:
1 A root (zero) of the function \(y = f(x)\) is a value of \(x\) for which:
(Function \(y = f(x)\) ka root (zero, jazr) \(x\) ki woh qeemat hai jis ke liye:)
blocks.explanation: Root woh \(x\) hai jis par \(y = f(x) = 0\) ho, yaani \(f(x) = 0\) ka hal.

book_ref.quote: A root (or zero) of a function

blocks.prompt:
2 Geometrically, a real root of \(y = f(x)\) is shown by the point where the graph of \(f\):
(Geometry mein \(y = f(x)\) ka real root graph ke kis point se zahir hota hai?)

options.text: line y = x ko milta hai

blocks.explanation: Root \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = 0\) ka mushtarak hal hai; \(y = 0\) x-axis hai, is liye root wahan hai jahan graph x-axis ko milta hai.

book_ref.quote: the geometric representation of a root of the function

blocks.prompt:
3 The graph of \(y = f(x)\) meets the \(x\)-axis at the point \((3, 0)\). Then a root of \(f\) is:
(\(y = f(x)\) ka graph x-axis ko point \((3, 0)\) par milta hai. To \(f\) ka root kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Root number \(x = 3\) hai (kyun ke \(f(3) = 0\)); \((3, 0)\) graph ka point hai.

book_ref.quote: Two ways of seeing the same root

blocks.prompt:
4 Which one of the following is a nonlinear equation?
(In mein se kaun si nonlinear equation (ghair-khatti muadla) hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(x + e^{x}\) ko \(ax + b\) ki shakal mein nahin likh sakte kyun ke \(x\) exponential ke andar hai. Baqi teeno \(ax + b = 0\) hain.

book_ref.quote: the variable may appear with powers greater than one or inside trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic or other nonlinear functions

blocks.prompt:
5 The roots of \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2x - 8\) are:
(\(f(x) = x^{2} - 2x - 8\) ke roots kya hain?)

book_ref.quote: A nonlinear equation is an equation of the form

blocks.prompt:
6 No general algebraic formula exists for the roots of polynomial equations of degree:
(Kis degree ki polynomial equations ke roots ka koi aam algebraic formula mojood nahin?)
blocks.explanation: Quadratic, cubic aur quartic ke formulas mojood hain, lekin degree 5 (quintic) ya us se zyada ke liye koi aam formula nahin.

book_ref.quote: no general algebraic formula is available for quintic or higher-degree polynomials

blocks.prompt:
7 A linear equation \(ax + b = 0\) with \(a \ne 0\) has:
(Linear equation \(ax + b = 0\), \(a \ne 0\), ke kitne roots hain?)
blocks.explanation: \(ax + b = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\frac{b}{a}\), sirf aik root. Nonlinear equation ke koi, aik ya bohat se roots ho sakte hain.

book_ref.quote: May have no root, one root or many roots

blocks.prompt:
8 A true root is \(-2.4567\ldots\). Correct to two decimal places it is written as:
(Asal root \(-2.4567\ldots\) hai. Do decimal places tak sahi likhein to:)
blocks.explanation: Teesra decimal 6 hai (\(\ge 5\)), is liye doosra decimal barhta hai: \(-2.46\). \(-2.45\) sirf kaatna hai, rounding nahin.

book_ref.quote: Always keep more decimals in your working (at least 4) and round only at the end.

blocks.prompt:
9 The Location of Root Theorem (LRT) can be applied to f on [a, b] when:
(Location of Root Theorem (LRT) f par [a, b] mein kab lagaya ja sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: LRT: agar \(f\) band interval \([a, b]\) par continuous (musalsal) ho aur \(f(a)f(b) < 0\) (ulte signs), to \(]a, b[\) mein root hai.

book_ref.quote: real-valued function which is continuous on a closed interval

blocks.prompt:
10 If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(f(a)f(b) < 0\), then in \(]a, b[\) the function \(f\) has:
(Agar \(f\), \([a, b]\) par continuous ho aur \(f(a)f(b) < 0\), to \(]a, b[\) mein \(f\) ke:)

options.text: kam az kam aik real root

blocks.explanation: LRT kam az kam aik root ki zamanat deta hai; curve axis ko teen (ya koi taaq tadaad) baar bhi kaat sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: The theorem promises one, not exactly one.

blocks.prompt:
11 Which one is an interval of sign change for \(f(x) = x^{3} - 6x + 2\)?
(\(f(x) = x^{3} - 6x + 2\) ke liye sign change ka interval kaun sa hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(f(0) = 2\), \(f(1) = -3\): signs ulte, is liye \([0, 1]\). Baqi intervals par signs aik jaise hain: \(-3, -2\); \(11, 42\); \(6, 7\).

book_ref.quote: an interval of sign change for the function

blocks.prompt:
12 For \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 2}\), \(f(1) = -1\) and \(f(3) = 1\), yet \(f\) has no root in \(]1, 3[\). The reason is:
(\(f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 2}\) mein \(f(1) = -1\), \(f(3) = 1\), phir bhi \(]1, 3[\) mein koi root nahin. Wajah:)

options.text: LRT bilkul aik root deta hai

blocks.explanation: LRT ke liye \([1, 3]\) par continuity zaroori hai; \(x = 2\) par \(\frac{1}{x - 2}\) defined nahin, graph wahan toot jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Continuity cannot be dropped.

blocks.prompt:
13 \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(f(a)f(b) > 0\). Which statement is correct?
(\(f\), \([a, b]\) par continuous hai aur \(f(a)f(b) > 0\). Kaun sa bayan durust hai?)

options.text: LRT koi natija nahin deta; \(]a, b[\) mein root ho bhi sakta hai, nahin bhi

blocks.explanation: Kinaron par aik jaise signs roots ko khatam nahin karte: \((x - 1)(x - 2)\) ki qeemat \(x = 0\) aur \(x = 3\) par \(2\) hai, magar beech mein roots \(1, 2\) hain.

book_ref.quote: No sign change does not mean no root.

blocks.explanation: Sign chaar alag intervals \([-4, -2]\), \([-2, 0]\), \([0, 2]\), \([2, 4]\) par badalta hai, is liye kam az kam 4 roots (\(\pm 1, \pm 3\)).

book_ref.quote: Separate (non-overlapping) intervals of sign change give separate roots

blocks.prompt:
15 For \(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 5\), the value of \(f(1)f(2)\) and the conclusion are:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 5\) ke liye \(f(1)f(2)\) ki qeemat aur natija:)
blocks.explanation: \(f(1) = -3\), \(f(2) = 5\); \(f(1)f(2) = -15 < 0\) aur polynomial continuous hai, is liye LRT se \(]1, 2[\) mein root hai.

book_ref.quote: A product is negative only when one factor is negative and the other positive

blocks.prompt:
16 A continuous function has \(f(2) = -3\) and \(f(5) = 4\). Which must be true?
(Aik continuous function ke liye \(f(2) = -3\) aur \(f(5) = 4\). Kya laazmi durust hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(f(2)f(5) = -12 < 0\) aur \(f\) continuous hai, is liye graph \(]2, 5[\) mein kisi \(c\) par axis kaatta hai; zaroori nahin ke 3.5 par.

book_ref.quote: its graph can be drawn without lifting the pencil from the paper

blocks.text: 8.2 Graphical Method for Approximating Real Roots

blocks.prompt:
17 The graphical method is mainly suitable for a root correct to:
(Graphical method aam tor par root ko kitne decimal places tak dene ke liye munasib hai?)
blocks.explanation: Graph aankh se parha jata hai, is liye sirf aik ya do decimal places; phir 8.3 ke methods behtar karte hain.

book_ref.quote: is mainly suitable for obtaining the root correct up to one or two decimal places

blocks.prompt:
18 In this unit the graphical method is mainly used to:
(Is unit mein graphical method zyada tar kis kaam aata hai?)

options.text: Bisection, Regula-Falsi aur Newton-Raphson ke liye shuru ki qeemat dena

blocks.explanation: Yeh pehla andaza (aik do decimals) deta hai jise iterative methods behtar karte hain.

book_ref.quote: used to provide an initial estimate for numerical methods

blocks.prompt:
19 For \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\), \(f(1.4) = -0.04\) and \(f(1.5) = 0.25\). The graph of \(f\) crosses the \(x\)-axis between:
(\(f(x) = x^{2} - 2\) ke liye \(f(1.4) = -0.04\), \(f(1.5) = 0.25\). Graph x-axis ko kahan kaatta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sign 1.4 aur 1.5 ke darmiyan \(-\) se \(+\) hota hai, is liye crossing \(]1.4, 1.5[\) mein hai (\(\sqrt{2} = 1.414\ldots\)).

book_ref.quote: within the interval of sign change only

blocks.prompt:
20 While tabulating \(f(x) = x - 2\sin x\), the value of \(\sin 0.5\) to be used is:
(\(f(x) = x - 2\sin x\) ki table banate waqt \(\sin 0.5\) ki kaun si qeemat leni hai?)
blocks.explanation: Radian mode: \(\sin 0.5 = 0.4794\). \(0.0087\) degree mode ka \(\sin 0.5^{\circ}\) hai aur \(0.8776\) \(\cos 0.5\) hai.

book_ref.quote: always keep your calculator in radian mode

blocks.prompt:
21 For \(f(x) = 2x - e^{-x}\): \(f(0.3) = -0.1408\) and \(f(0.4) = 0.1297\). Treating the curve as nearly straight between these points, the root to two decimal places is about:
(\(f(x) = 2x - e^{-x}\): \(f(0.3) = -0.1408\), \(f(0.4) = 0.1297\). Yahan curve ko taqreeban seedha samjhein to root do decimal places tak taqreeban:)
blocks.explanation: Curve 0.1 ke qadam mein \(0.2705\) barhti hai; 0 tak \(\frac{0.1408}{0.2705} \approx 0.52\) hissa: \(0.3 + 0.052 \approx 0.35\) (asal root \(0.3517\)).

book_ref.quote: This method provides a visual way to locate where a function crosses

blocks.text: 8.3 Numerical Methods for Solving Nonlinear Equations

blocks.prompt:
22 Which methods start from an interval of sign change and keep the root trapped inside it?
(Kaun se methods sign change ke interval se shuru hote hain aur root ko us ke andar band rakhte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Bisection aur Regula-Falsi dono [a, b] par sign change chahte hain; Newton-Raphson aik qeemat x0 se shuru hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Bisection and Regula-Falsi start from an interval of sign change

blocks.prompt:
23 Bisection, Regula-Falsi and Newton-Raphson are called iterative methods because:
(Bisection, Regula-Falsi aur Newton-Raphson ko iterative methods kyun kehte hain?)

options.text: aik hi qadam mein exact root dete hain
har qadam pichle andaze se behtar andaza deta hai, kafi durusti tak dohraya jata hai
sirf polynomials ke liye kaam karte hain

blocks.explanation: Iterative ka matlab aik hi qadam baar baar; har baar andaza behtar hota hai jab tak tolerance poori na ho.

book_ref.quote: each step improves the estimate of the root

blocks.prompt:
24 Which method needs the derivative of f?
(Kis method mein f ka derivative (mushtaq) chahiye?)
blocks.explanation: Newton-Raphson tangent istemal karta hai: \(x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}\). Baqi do sirf \(f\) ki qeematein lete hain.

book_ref.quote: These methods use the concept of intervals where the function changes sign

blocks.text: 8.3.1 General Rule of Accuracy, Tolerance and Calculator Setup

blocks.prompt:
25 For a root correct to 3 decimal places, the stopping tolerance is:
(3 decimal places tak sahi root ke liye stopping tolerance kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: is the number of decimal places required for the root

blocks.prompt:
26 For a root correct to 4 decimal places, the tolerance is:
(4 decimal places ke liye tolerance kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: we will follow the function value criterion

blocks.prompt:
27 To obtain a root correct to 2 decimal places, the least number of decimal places the calculator should be fixed to during the working is:
(2 decimal places tak root ke liye hal ke dauran calculator kam az kam kitne decimal places par set ho?)
blocks.explanation: Kam az kam \(n + 1 = 3\) decimal places; sirf aakhri jawab 2 tak round karein.

book_ref.quote: decimal places through all the intermediate calculations and round the final answer to the required accuracy

blocks.prompt:
28 Which value of \(|f(c)|\) allows us to stop for a root correct to 2 decimal places?
(2 decimal places ke liye \(|f(c)|\) ki kaun si qeemat par ruk sakte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Shart \(|f(c)| < 0.005\) hai. Sirf \(0.0041\) is se kam hai.

book_ref.quote: can move a number by at most half a unit of the last place

blocks.prompt:
29 For one decimal place (\(n = 1\)) the tolerance \(\frac{10^{-n}}{2}\) equals:
(Aik decimal place (\(n = 1\)) ke liye tolerance \(\frac{10^{-n}}{2}\) kitni hai?)

book_ref.quote: Use radian mode if trigonometric functions are involved.

blocks.prompt:
30 In the bisection method on \([1.2, 2]\), the first estimate of the root is:
(Bisection method mein \([1.2, 2]\) par root ka pehla andaza kya hai?)

book_ref.quote: The method systematically halves the interval to narrow down the location of the root

blocks.prompt:
31 In a bisection step \(f(a) < 0\), \(f(b) > 0\) and \(f(c) > 0\) at the midpoint \(c\). The next interval is:
(Bisection ke qadam mein \(f(a) < 0\), \(f(b) > 0\) aur midpoint par \(f(c) > 0\). Agla interval:)
blocks.explanation: \(f(a)f(c) < 0\), is liye root \([a, c]\) mein hai: \(b = c\) rakhein.

book_ref.quote: How to decide which half to keep: look only at signs.

blocks.prompt:
32 Bisection on \(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 1\) over \([0, 1]\): \(f(0.5) = -0.375\). The interval for the next step is:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 1\) par \([0, 1]\) mein bisection: \(f(0.5) = -0.375\). Agle qadam ka interval:)

book_ref.quote: a simple and reliable numerical technique to find roots of nonlinear equations in one variable

blocks.prompt:
33 Bisection starts on \([0, 1]\). After 6 halvings, the length of the interval containing the root is:
(Bisection \([0, 1]\) se shuru. 6 baar aadha karne ke baad root wale interval ki lambai:)
blocks.explanation: \(k\) qadmon ke baad lambai \(\frac{b - a}{2^{k}} = \frac{1}{64}\).

book_ref.quote: After \(k\) steps the interval has length

blocks.prompt:
34 Bisection on \(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x - 5\) over \([2, 3]\) gives \(f(2.5) = 5.625\). The second midpoint is:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x - 5\) par \([2, 3]\) mein bisection: \(f(2.5) = 5.625\). Doosra midpoint:)

book_ref.quote: Repeat Steps 2–3 until \(|f(c)|\) is near zero.

blocks.explanation: Pehle qadam ke baad \([1.5, 2]\), doosre ke baad \([1.5, 1.75]\); is liye \(c_3 = 1.625\).

book_ref.quote: That is why bisection always works, but slowly.

blocks.prompt:
36 Starting on \([1, 2]\), the least number of bisection steps that makes the interval length less than \(0.01\) is:
(\([1, 2]\) se shuru karke kam az kam kitne bisection qadmon se interval ki lambai \(0.01\) se kam hogi?)

book_ref.quote: It always converges, but slowly: the interval only halves at each step.

blocks.prompt:
37 The Regula-Falsi estimate of the root in [a, b] is:
([a, b] mein root ka Regula-Falsi andaza kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh secant line ka x-intercept hai: har end point doosre end ki \(f\) se zarb hota hai. \(\frac{a + b}{2}\) bisection ka midpoint hai.

book_ref.quote: using the Regula-Falsi formula

blocks.prompt:
38 In the Regula-Falsi method the new estimate c is the point where the x-axis is cut by:
(Regula-Falsi mein naya andaza c woh point hai jahan x-axis ko kaatti hai:)

options.text: (a, f(a)) aur (b, f(b)) se guzarne wali secant line

blocks.explanation: Regula-Falsi end points ko seedhi line (secant) se jorta hai aur us ka x-intercept leta hai.

book_ref.quote: The idea of Regula-Falsi is to approximate the root by drawing a straight line through the points

blocks.prompt:
39 The slope of the secant line through \((a, f(a))\) and \((b, f(b))\) is:
(\((a, f(a))\) aur \((b, f(b))\) se guzarne wali secant line ka slope:)
blocks.explanation: Slope = \(y\) ki tabdeeli / \(x\) ki tabdeeli = \(\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}\).

book_ref.quote: Slope of the secant line passing through the points

blocks.prompt:
40 The first Regula-Falsi estimate for \(f(x) = x^{2} - 3\) on \([1, 2]\) is:
(\(f(x) = x^{2} - 3\) ke liye \([1, 2]\) par pehla Regula-Falsi andaza:)

book_ref.quote: Bisection and Regula-Falsi differ only in Step 2

blocks.prompt:
41 The first Regula-Falsi estimate for \(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x - 5\) on \([2, 3]\) is:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x - 5\) ke liye \([2, 3]\) par pehla Regula-Falsi andaza:)

book_ref.quote: Write negative values in brackets when substituting

blocks.prompt:
42 The first Regula-Falsi estimate for \(f(x) = x^{3} - 5x + 1\) on \([0, 1]\) is:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} - 5x + 1\) ke liye \([0, 1]\) par pehla Regula-Falsi andaza:)
blocks.explanation: \(f(0) = 1\), \(f(1) = -3\): \(c = \frac{-1}{-4} = 0.25\); yeh 0 ke qareeb hai jahan \(|f|\) chhota hai.

book_ref.quote: the secant takes this into account, the midpoint does not

blocks.prompt:
43 For \(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 1\) on \([0, 1]\), \(f(0) = -1\) and \(f(1) = 1\). The first Regula-Falsi estimate is:
(\(f(x) = x^{3} + x - 1\), \([0, 1]\): \(f(0) = -1\), \(f(1) = 1\). Pehla Regula-Falsi andaza:)
blocks.explanation: \(c = \frac{0 + 1}{2} = 0.5\). Jab \(f(a) = -f(b)\) ho to secant bilkul midpoint par kaatti hai.

book_ref.quote: Often one end never moves

blocks.prompt:
44 Compared with the bisection method, the Regula-Falsi method:
(Bisection ke muqable mein Regula-Falsi method:)

options.text: aam tor par tez hai, aur root ko sign change ke interval mein band rakhta hai
root ko kabhi interval mein nahin rakhta
hamesha sirf aik iteration leta hai

blocks.explanation: Dono root ko sign change se band rakhte hain; Regula-Falsi midpoint ki jagah secant ka x-intercept leta hai jo aam tor par root ke zyada qareeb hota hai.

book_ref.quote: It is usually faster than bisection

blocks.prompt:
45 The Newton-Raphson formula is:
(Newton-Raphson formula kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Tangent \(y - f(x_n) = f'(x_n)(x - x_n)\) mein \(y = 0\) se \(x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}\) (minus ka nishan).

book_ref.quote: This method works by drawing a tangent to the curve

blocks.prompt:
46 The tangent to \(y = f(x)\) at \((x_0, f(x_0))\) used in the Newton-Raphson method is:
(Newton-Raphson mein \((x_0, f(x_0))\) par \(y = f(x)\) ka tangent:)
blocks.explanation: Slope \(f'(x_0)\) aur line \((x_0, f(x_0))\) se guzarti hai: point-slope form.

book_ref.quote: The slope of the tangent line to the curve

blocks.prompt:
47 For \(f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 1\), at which starting value does the Newton-Raphson formula break down?
(\(f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 1\) ke liye kis shuru ki qeemat par Newton-Raphson formula kaam nahin karta?)
blocks.explanation: \(f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 12\); \(f'(2) = 0\) (ufuqi tangent, sifar se taqseem). Baqi par \(f' \ne 0\).

book_ref.quote: should not be zero near the root

blocks.prompt:
48 Newton-Raphson for \(f(x) = x^{2} - 3\) with \(x_0 = 2\) gives \(x_1 =\)
(\(f(x) = x^{2} - 3\), \(x_0 = 2\) se Newton-Raphson ka \(x_1\):)

book_ref.quote: A zero slope means a horizontal tangent, which never meets the x-axis

blocks.prompt:
49 Applied to \(f(x) = x^{2} - 7\), the Newton-Raphson formula simplifies to:
(\(f(x) = x^{2} - 7\) par Newton-Raphson formula sada ho kar:)

book_ref.quote: Repeating this process produces a sequence of

blocks.prompt:
50 For the cube root of 7 we solve \(f(x) = x^{3} - 7 = 0\). The Newton-Raphson formula becomes:
(7 ka cube root: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 7 = 0\). Newton-Raphson formula ban jata hai:)

book_ref.quote: the number of correct decimals roughly doubles at each step
This tangent intersects the

blocks.prompt:
52 To solve \(e^{x} = 3x\) by Newton-Raphson from \(x_0 = 0\), the value of \(x_1\) is:
(\(e^{x} = 3x\) ko Newton-Raphson se \(x_0 = 0\) se hal karein to \(x_1\):)

book_ref.quote: Write the given equation in the form

blocks.prompt:
53 Which statement about the Newton-Raphson method is correct?
(Newton-Raphson method ke bare mein kaun sa bayan durust hai?)

options.text: Root hamesha do end points ke darmiyan rehta hai
Bura shuru ka andaza root se door le ja sakta hai, kyun ke root interval mein band nahin hota

blocks.explanation: Newton-Raphson aik qeemat se tangents ke zariye chalta hai; aam tor par sab se tez, magar bura x0 root se door le ja sakta hai.

book_ref.quote: This method does not rely directly on the Location of Root Theorem (LRT).

blocks.prompt:
54 Newton-Raphson for \(f(x) = \cos x - 2x\) with \(x_0 = 0\) gives \(x_1 =\)
(\(f(x) = \cos x - 2x\), \(x_0 = 0\) se \(x_1\):)

book_ref.quote: Unlike bisection and Regula-Falsi, the root is not trapped in an interval

blocks.text: 8.4 Estimating the Value of a Definite Integral

blocks.prompt:
55 Which definite integral cannot be evaluated by elementary methods and is estimated numerically?
(Kaun sa definite integral elementary tareeqon se nahin nikalta aur numerically andaza lagaya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin(x^{2})\) ka koi elementary antiderivative nahin. Baqi: \(u = x^{2}\) substitution se, aur \(e^{x}\) seedha.

book_ref.quote: definite integrals are not always easy to evaluate analytically

blocks.prompt:
56 For a positive continuous function \(f\), the value \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx\) represents:
(Positive continuous \(f\) ke liye \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx\) kya zahir karta hai?)

options.text: x = a par curve ka slope
x = a se x = b tak curve aur x-axis ke darmiyan ka area

blocks.explanation: Positive continuous function ka definite integral graph ke neeche ka area hai; formula na bhi ho to yeh area aik mukarrar number hai.

book_ref.quote: The integral itself still exists.

blocks.prompt:
57 \([1, 3]\) is divided into \(n = 8\) equal subintervals. The width \(h\) is:
(\([1, 3]\) ko \(n = 8\) barabar hisson mein taqseem kiya. \(h\) kitna hai?)

book_ref.quote: for some positive integer \(n\). Divide the interval

blocks.prompt:
58 For \(\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx\) with \(h = 0.4\), the number of subintervals and of points are:
(\(\int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx\), \(h = 0.4\): subintervals aur points ki tadaad:)
blocks.explanation: \(n = \frac{2}{0.4} = 5\); \(n\) subintervals ke \(n + 1 = 6\) points hote hain.

book_ref.quote: Counting points as subintervals

blocks.prompt:
59 The Trapezium Rule states:
(Trapezium Rule kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(n\) trapeziums ke areas jama: kinare ki qeematein aik baar, andar wali do baar, sab ko \(\frac{h}{2}\) se zarb.

book_ref.quote: is approximately equal to the sum of areas of the trapeziums

blocks.prompt:
